title: PRD: Consumption Experience Journey Matrix
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This PRD defines the Consumption Experience Journey Matrix (CEJM): a single canonical mapping from customer-facing user journeys to the platform consumption mechanics (fidelity, routing, billing unit, SLOs, telemetry and operator controls). The CEJM will be used by Product, Runtime, Billing, and Developer Experience teams to:
- Ensure consistent UX to consumption mapping for new features
- Drive predictable billing language in docs and contracts
- Provide instrumentation and acceptance criteria for quality gates and rollouts

Context:
Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with many ways to trade cost vs latency vs quality (fidelity). Engineering teams have asked for a concise artifact that ties common application patterns to recommended configurations and telemetry so builders and account teams can quickly choose the right defaults and measure impact.

Goals

Primary goals:
1) Create a lightweight, canonical matrix that maps 8 priority user journeys to platform primitives (route, fidelity tier, billing unit).
2) Provide measurable acceptance criteria (SLOs) and telemetry contract for each row.
3) Define rollout plan and feature-flagging behavior for default changes.
4) Make the artifact consumable for sales and support to communicate economics to customers.

Non-goals:
- Replace detailed capacity sizing calculators or all pricing documents.
- Provide fine-grained per-tenant price negotiations (handled by enterprise playbooks).

Scope

Included:
- Interactive conversational workloads (chat, assistant flows)
- Transactional short completions (search/rerank/high-throughput APIs)
- Bulk/async embeddings pipelines
- Background reranking and summarization jobs
- Developer sandbox/experimentation flows
- Onboarding flow guidance and default feature flags

Excluded:
- Edge/offline runtime packaging (edge runtime will reference this matrix but is out of scope)
- Marketplace third-party variant pricing (separate catalog)

Prioritized User Journeys and Mapping

Please refer to the matrix below. This is the canonical table that should be referenced by UX copy, quickstarts, and contract templates.

| Journey ID | Typical product example | Primary route | Default fidelity tier | Billing unit | Representative SLO / Threshold | Telemetry events (required) | Default rollback policy | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| J-01 | Consumer chat assistant (single-turn + short context) | hosted-latency-optimized | standard | per-token | p95 generation latency < 200ms; error rate < 0.5% | chat.request.start, chat.token.stream, chat.request.end, chat.fidelity.negotiated | canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%; revert on p95 > 300ms | Conservative fidelity; low cost sensitivity |
| J-02 | Multi-turn assistant (context window 2–8k tokens) | hosted-fidelity-balanced | high | per-token | p95 end-to-end latency < 350ms; request success > 99% | chat.session.create, chat.kv.cache.hit, chat.fidelity.degraded | progressive canary with KV-cache priming |
| J-03 | Transactional completion (search snippet / fill) | dedicated-low-latency | trimmed | per-request | p99 < 120ms for single-turn short responses | completion.request, completion.latency, completion.fail | route to pre-warmed dedicated pool; fallback to hosted-trimmed |
| J-04 | Large-batch embeddings job (overnight) | async-batch | high-precision | per-embedding | throughput >= 1000 emb/s per job node; job success > 99% | embeddings.job.enqueue, embeddings.chunk.success, embeddings.job.complete | schedule to batch cluster during off-peak |
| J-05 | Reranking pipeline (mid latency, high accuracy) | dedicated-fidelity | high | per-token + per-request | p95 latency < 500ms; ranking p@10 degradation < 1% vs baseline | rerank.request, rerank.latency, rerank.quality.delta | prefer quantized high-fidelity variant |
| J-06 | Background summarization (async) | async-spot | standard | per-request (time-windowed) | job completion within SLA (24h) | summarization.job.start, summarization.job.complete | low priority, preemptible |
| J-07 | Developer experiment / sandbox | dev-sandbox | exploratory | per-token (trial credits) | p95 < 500ms; usage throttled to 10 RPS | devsandbox.session.start, devsandbox.quota.exhausted | auto-reset daily; explicit opt-in to higher fidelity |
| J-08 | Onboarding preflight cost estimate (simulation only) | simulator | fidelity-sim | simulation-run | accuracy within 10% of billed estimate | simulator.run.start, simulator.estimate.complete | read-only simulation; no billing incurred |

API surface and UX changes required

- New optional parameter: consumption_profile (string enum): ["latency-optimized", "fidelity-balanced", "fidelity-high", "batch-async", "exploratory"]. Default behavior: if omitted, server will map to the matrix row based on request attributes (route & client entitlements).
- SDK defaults: quickstart templates will pass consumption_profile for each SDK sample (chat, completion, embeddings).
- Console: expose a per-route preview of estimated cost impact when switching consumption_profile (delta in $/1M tokens or embeddings).

Telemetry & Metric Contracts

All rows require the following telemetry fields (platform-standard event schema):
- request_id (string)
- customer_id (string)
- route_id (string)
- journey_id (string)
- consumption_profile (string)
- fidelity_tier (string)
- tokens_in / tokens_out (int)
- latency_ms_p50, p95, p99 (ints)

Metrics to be emitted to dashboards (names for Grafana/Signal):
- redwood.journey.<journey_id>.request.count
- redwood.journey.<journey_id>.latency.p95_ms
- redwood.journey.<journey_id>.error_rate
- redwood.journey.<journey_id>.fidelity.delta_quality (for quality-focused journeys)
- billing.estimate.<route_id>.dollar_per_1M_tokens

Acceptance criteria (must pass before 100% rollout)

1) Instrumentation completeness: for each Journey row, >= 99% of requests must contain the required telemetry fields for 7 consecutive days in canary region.
2) Performance: observed p95 latency during 10k synthetic sessions must be <= defined threshold for the journey.
3) Cost estimate accuracy: simulator runs for 5 representative customers must predict billed delta within 15%.
4) UX clarity: quickstart and console cost preview copy approved by Product Marketing and Legal.

Rollout Plan and Feature Flags

1) Implement server-side consumption_profile support behind FF:ff.consultation.consumption_profile (default off).
2) Backfill telemetry for historic requests for two weeks post-launch for gap analysis.
3) Internal canary (10% of internal traffic) for 48 hours. Validate metrics and acceptance criteria.
4) Customer canary: invite 5 early-adopter customers (mix of SMB and enterprise) for 2 weeks. Monitor billing deviations and QA metrics.
5) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks if no regressions.

Feature flag behaviors:
- If canary metrics degrade (p95 increases > 30% of threshold or error rate > 1%), automatic rollback to previous mapping and alert oncall.
- Admin override in Console to pin a route to a specific consumption_profile.

Dependencies

- Billing: accurate $/token and $/embedding cost models for each fidelity variant.
- Runtime: implementation of consumption_profile mapping and routing logic.
- Telemetry: event schema rollout and low-latency collector.
- Console: cost preview UI and admin override control.
- Legal/Product Marketing: approved wording for cost preview and simulation disclaimers.

Risk assessment and mitigations

- Risk: Incorrect cost estimates leading to customer disputes.
  Mitigation: Hold customer canary cohorts and include an explicit "simulation" disclaimer. Provide instrumentation for billed vs estimated reconciliation.
- Risk: Unexpected latency regressions when a new fidelity mapping is used.
  Mitigation: Require automated synthetic load tests and live canary gating.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps reduce observability.
  Mitigation: Block rollout until instrumentation completeness acceptance criteria met.

Operational runbook snippets

1) If journey p95 exceeds threshold for a route:
   a) Check redwood.journey.<journey_id>.latency.p95_ms and recent deploys.
   b) Toggle route to previous consumption_profile via Console admin override.
   c) Page Runtime oncall if rollback does not reduce p95 within 5m.

2) If billed delta deviates > 25% vs simulator for a customer:
   a) Open internal billing investigation ticket and notify Customer Success.
   b) Temporarily pin the customer's route to a lower-cost consumption_profile until resolved.

Appendix: example request payload (SDK change)

Python (pseudo) example:

client.chat.create(
    model="redwood-chat-l1",
    messages=[{"role":"user", "content":"Summarize this..."}],
    consumption_profile="latency-optimized"  # optional; defaults to matrix mapping
)

Telemetry sample (JSON event)

{
  "event": "chat.request.end",
  "request_id": "req-8a7c9",
  "customer_id": "acct-412",
  "journey_id": "J-01",
  "consumption_profile": "latency-optimized",
  "fidelity_tier": "standard",
  "tokens_in": 24,
  "tokens_out": 128,
  "latency_ms_p95": 142
}

Ownership and next steps

- Product (owner): finalize matrix and UX copy; coordinate reviewers.
- Runtime (owner): implement server-side switch, routing and fallback policies.
- Billing (owner): publish cost model endpoints and simulator integration.
- DX (owner): update quickstarts and SDK examples.

Next milestones:
- 2026-07-29: Implementation RFC and telemetry schema PR merged.
- 2026-08-12: Internal canary and synthetic validation complete.
- 2026-08-26: Customer canary start.
- 2026-09-09: General availability (GA) decision meeting.
